subject: biology
title: Anaerobic respiration and fermentation
key_idea: Anaerobic respiration releases energy from glucose without oxygen. Muscles make lactic acid. Plant and yeast cells make ethanol and carbon dioxide. It releases much less energy than aerobic respiration, because the glucose is only partly broken down.

blocks.text: During vigorous exercise the blood cannot supply oxygen fast enough. Muscle cells then respire anaerobically as well as aerobically.

items.meaning: Respiration without oxygen. It still transfers energy from glucose.
The product of anaerobic respiration in animal muscle cells.

blocks.label: Anaerobic respiration in muscles
where: lactic acid is the only product, so no carbon dioxide or water is made

blocks.text: The oxidation of glucose is incomplete, so much less energy is transferred than in aerobic respiration.

items: Muscles respire anaerobically when they do not have enough oxygen.
Glucose is broken down to lactic acid, with no carbon dioxide or water.
Much less energy is transferred, because the glucose is only partly broken down.

sections.heading: Anaerobic respiration in plants and yeast

blocks.text: Plant cells and yeast cells make different products from animal cells when they respire without oxygen.

blocks.label: Anaerobic respiration in plant and yeast cells

blocks.text: Anaerobic respiration in yeast cells is called **fermentation**. It has economic importance.

items: Bread making: the carbon dioxide makes the dough rise, so the bread is lighter.
Alcoholic drinks such as beer and wine: yeast ferments sugar to make ethanol.
Fermentation is controlled by enzymes. It does not work if it is too cold for the enzymes, and the enzymes are denatured if it is too hot.

diagram.alt: Pick a type of cell and its conditions to see what respiration it carries out, what it makes and how much energy is released.
diagram.prompt: Pick a cell and its conditions

options.label: Muscle cell, plenty of oxygen
options.explanation: Glucose is broken down completely using oxygen.

options.label: Muscle cell, not enough oxygen
options.explanation: The glucose is only partly broken down, so lactic acid builds up.

options.label: Yeast cell, no oxygen
options.explanation: Fermentation is used to make bread and alcoholic drinks.

options.label: Plant cell, no oxygen
options.explanation: Plant cells make the same products as yeast.

items: Plants and yeast make ethanol and carbon dioxide. Animal muscles make lactic acid.
Fermentation in yeast makes bread rise and makes alcoholic drinks.
Fermentation needs enzymes, so temperature matters.

blocks.text: Exam questions ask you to compare the types of respiration. Learn the oxygen, the products and the energy released.

items: Anaerobic respiration releases less energy because the glucose is not completely broken down.
Aerobic makes carbon dioxide and water. Anaerobic never makes water.

checks.q: Write the word equation for anaerobic respiration in muscle cells.
Which two substances are made by anaerobic respiration in plant cells?
Explain why anaerobic respiration is less efficient than aerobic respiration.
checks.a: Less energy is released per molecule of glucose, because the glucose is only partly broken down (incomplete oxidation).

worked_example.question:
An athlete ran on a running machine, reaching maximum intensity of exercise and then stopping. During the exercise the athlete respired aerobically and anaerobically.

Explain why anaerobic respiration is less efficient than aerobic respiration.
answer_points: Less energy is released or transferred per molecule of glucose (allow: more glucose must be broken down to release the same energy).
Because the breakdown or oxidation of glucose is incomplete (allow: glucose is only broken down to lactic acid).
worked_example.tip: Say energy is released or transferred, never produced, made or created. "No energy released" is not accepted.

worked_example.question:
Respiration occurs in cells. An athlete runs every day as part of their training.

When the athlete is running, their muscle cells use both aerobic respiration and anaerobic respiration.

State two differences between aerobic respiration and anaerobic respiration.
answer_points: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen, anaerobic respiration does not.
Aerobic respiration releases more energy, anaerobic releases less.
Aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water, anaerobic produces lactic acid.
Aerobic respiration takes place in the mitochondria, anaerobic in the cytoplasm.
worked_example.tip: Any two of the four points score. ATP is accepted for energy and lactate for lactic acid.

worked_example.question:
Yeast cells can respire anaerobically.

Write down two ways in which anaerobic respiration in yeast cells is different from anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells.
answer_points: Alcohol (ethanol) is produced in yeast but not in humans.
Lactic acid is produced by humans but not by yeast.
Carbon dioxide is produced by yeast but not by humans.
worked_example.tip: Any two points. If any incorrect product is stated the answer is limited to one mark. Oxygen debt and ATP are ignored.

worked_example.question:
Human muscle cells use anaerobic respiration during vigorous exercise.

Compare the process of anaerobic respiration to aerobic respiration in human muscle cells.
answer_points: Anaerobic respiration happens without oxygen. Aerobic respiration uses oxygen.
Anaerobic respiration releases less energy per glucose molecule.
Anaerobic respiration produces lactic acid. Aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water.
Anaerobic respiration does not happen in the mitochondria.
Both types of respiration use glucose.
worked_example.tip: Any three of the points earn the three marks. Give a difference each time.

items: The ethanol can be used as a **biofuel**.
In bread-making, the carbon dioxide from yeast makes the dough rise.

worked_example.question:
A horse breathes faster and deeper when running.

Explain why the horse continues to breathe faster and deeper for a period of time after it has stopped running.
answer_points: Anaerobic respiration had happened, so lactic acid built up.
The horse needs extra oxygen to break down the lactic acid (to repay the oxygen debt).
worked_example.tip: Any two of: more oxygen is needed, lactic acid is broken down, the oxygen debt is repaid, anaerobic respiration had happened.

blocks.text: This section covers a practical that shows yeast respiring anaerobically.

items.text: Put yeast in a glucose solution in a flask, and add a layer of oil to keep oxygen out.
Set up a second flask with no oil, so oxygen can reach the yeast.
Pass the gas from each flask into limewater, or count the bubbles in a set time.
The limewater goes cloudy and bubbles appear, because the yeast makes carbon dioxide.

items: Keep the temperature and the amount of yeast and glucose the same in each flask.
Anaerobic respiration by yeast also makes ethanol.
